title: Multiple testing with anytime-valid Monte Carlo p-values

split.decision: Original independent Gaussian standard cell: M=1000, pi_A=.4, mu_A=2.5, alpha=.1, B=10000, 10 trials; validation exactly set.seed(123) pis grid cell 4; test same DGP with independent private seed. Observed statistics only; frozen sampler carries null-stream state without truth.

allowed_changes: Adaptive query allocation, stopping, valid p-value/e-value construction, multiple-testing strategy and auxiliary fitting methods may change within the sampler-only information contract.
Besag-Clifford h=10 and sequential-BH implementation are baseline methods rather than mandatory algorithms.
When retaining the supplied sequential_BH code, changing only method="bc" (including its existing bm and AMT branches), param_bc=10 or peeking_times=1:B does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Reduce the actual Monte Carlo null-sampling cost of the specified multiple-testing problem while maintaining its fixed power and FDR thresholds.
Only supplied observed statistics and authorized raw null-sampler prefixes are admissible decision information; the null law cannot be replaced by analytic Gaussian knowledge or external draws.
Ten independent trials, M=1000, B=10000, alpha=.1, actual unique disclosed query cost, power>=.720 and FDR<=.10 remain fixed.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: No analytical normal p-values, extra simulated null samples, sampler-RNG recovery, inaccessible future prefixes, false query counts or cross-trial state.
Do not replace null hypotheses, change FDR/power definitions or submit known truth labels as decisions.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

Rejections must be supported by Monte Carlo p-values, e-values or another valid test calibrated from authorized null-sampler observations. A rule that rejects by an observed-statistic cutoff or rank chosen through validation selection, while ignoring the disclosed null samples, is not allowed. Patch audit enforces this.
